hero.title: You CAN Become a Data Engineer
hero.subtitle: No PhD required. Start from backend/fullstack and transition.
hero.description: Think Data Engineering is only for data scientists? Think again. I've helped software engineers, backend developers, and DBAs transition into Data Engineer roles at AWS, Google, Meta, and more. Here's your complete roadmap.

mythBusters.title: Breaking the Myths
mythBusters.subtitle: What's really stopping you isn't what you think

myths.myth: I need a PhD or Statistics background
myths.reality: Data Engineering focuses on building pipelines, not statistical modeling. Your software engineering skills are exactly what companies need. Most data engineers come from backend/fullstack backgrounds.

myths.myth: I need to know Machine Learning
myths.reality: Data Engineers build the infrastructure FOR ML teams, not the models. Focus on data pipelines, storage, and processing. ML knowledge is a nice-to-have, not a requirement.

myths.myth: I need Hadoop/Spark experience from day one
myths.reality: Start with SQL and Python. Add Spark when you're comfortable. Modern cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Snowflake) abstract much of the complexity. Learn incrementally.

myths.myth: Data Engineering is just ETL scripting
myths.reality: Modern Data Engineering involves distributed systems, real-time streaming, data governance, and platform architecture. It's highly technical and strategic.
Data Engineer demand is exploding. Every company needs to process and analyze data. The shortage of skilled data engineers means excellent compensation and job security.

faqs.question: Can I become a Data Engineer without a CS degree?
faqs.answer: Absolutely! Many successful Data Engineers come from non-CS backgrounds. What matters is your ability to learn SQL, Python, and understand data systems. Your analytical mindset and problem-solving skills are more important than your degree.

faqs.question: Should I learn Spark or focus on cloud-native tools?
faqs.answer: Learn both, but prioritize based on your target companies. Spark is still widely used and great for interviews. Cloud-native tools (AWS Glue, Dataflow) are increasingly popular. Start with cloud tools for faster wins, add Spark for depth.

faqs.question: How is Data Engineering different from Data Science?
faqs.answer: Data Engineers build the infrastructure and pipelines that move and transform data. Data Scientists analyze that data and build models. Think of it as: Data Engineers build the kitchen, Data Scientists cook the food. Both are essential.

faqs.question: What's the best certification for Data Engineering?
faqs.answer: AWS Data Analytics Specialty or GCP Professional Data Engineer are highly valued. Databricks certifications are also growing in popularity. Pick one aligned with your target companies and cloud preference.

faqs.question: How long does it take to transition to Data Engineering?
faqs.answer: With dedicated effort (1-2 hours daily), most software engineers can transition in 4-6 months. Your existing programming skills give you a head start. Focus on SQL, Python, and one cloud platform first.
